title: The Psychology of Feedback: How to Receive It (Without Falling Apart)

sentences.en: Sometimes we get so used to doing things a certain way that we forget there might be other possibilities.
sentences.zh: 有时候我们太习惯于某种做事方式，以至于忘记了可能还有其他选择。

sentences.en: That can most definitely apply to our working lives too.
sentences.zh: 这一点绝对也适用于我们的工作生活。

sentences.en: I'm Dr Marianne Trent and one of the biggest changes I've made in my career has been exploring ways to earn money beyond traditional one-to-one work.
sentences.zh: 我是 Marianne Trent 博士，我职业生涯中做出的最大改变之一，就是探索传统一对一工作之外的赚钱方式。

sentences.en: If that sparks your curiosity, Sophie Foote's free Race to Recurring
sentences.zh: 如果这激发了你的好奇心，Sophie Foote 的免费“通往经常性收入挑战”

sentences.en: Revenue Challenge starts on the 2nd of November.
sentences.zh: 将于 11 月 2 日开始。

sentences.en: I'd love you to join us.
sentences.zh: 我很希望你能加入我们。

sentences.en: You'll find my link in the show notes or you can drop me a DM via socials.
sentences.zh: 你可以在节目说明中找到我的链接，或者通过社交媒体给我发私信。

sentences.en: Now on with the show.
sentences.zh: 现在，继续我们的节目。

sentences.en: Why does receiving feedback about ourselves sometimes feel like a personal attack even when we know it's meant to help us?
sentences.zh: 为什么收到关于我们自己的反馈时，即使我们知道那是为了帮助我们，有时也会感觉像是一种人身攻击？

sentences.en: In this episode we're unpacking the psychology of feedback.
sentences.zh: 在这一集中，我们将剖析反馈背后的心理学。

sentences.en: Why it stings, why we avoid it and how learning to receive it well can transform our personal and professional growth.
sentences.zh: 为什么它会刺痛我们，为什么我们回避它，以及学会如何正确地接受反馈，如何改变我们的个人和职业成长。

sentences.en: Hope you find it super useful.
sentences.zh: 希望你觉得这非常有帮助。

sentences.en: Hi I'm Dr Marianne, a qualified clinical psychologist and I do love receiving your feedback.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是 Marianne 博士，一名合格的临床心理学家，我非常喜欢收到你们的反馈。

sentences.en: You can do that by dropping me a like or a comment, subscribing to the channel or by getting in contact and letting me know what you think to the content.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过点赞、评论、订阅频道，或者联系我告诉我你对内容的看法来做到这一点。

sentences.en: But I know that especially sometimes if it's unsolicited feedback we're offered, that doesn't always feel quite so nice.
sentences.zh: 但我知道，特别是当我们收到主动提供的反馈时，感觉并不总是那么好。

sentences.en: And I know when we're in a variety of roles especially if we're working in mental health that we need to be kind of aware of our impact on others.
sentences.zh: 而且我知道，当我们担任各种角色时，特别是在心理健康领域工作时，我们需要意识到自己对他人的影响。

sentences.en: We need to be kind of getting regular check-ins from our supervisors, often from our clients and our peers as well, about how we are doing.
sentences.zh: 我们需要定期从主管、客户以及同行那里获得关于我们表现的反馈。

sentences.en: But that doesn't always feel super comfortable.
sentences.zh: 但这并不总是让人感觉非常舒服。

sentences.en: Sometimes it can feel overwhelming, confusing, sometimes even painful.
sentences.zh: 有时它会让人感到不知所措、困惑，甚至痛苦。

sentences.en: So today we are exploring why this happens, how it can tie into our deep need for belonging and offering a few practical ways that can make feedback feel
sentences.zh: 所以今天我们要探讨为什么会发生这种情况，它如何与我们对归属感的深层需求联系起来，并提供一些实用的方法，让反馈感觉

sentences.en: less scary and more empowering.
sentences.zh: 不那么可怕，反而更具赋能作用。

sentences.en: Let's dive in.
sentences.zh: 让我们开始吧。

sentences.en: Number one, why feedback can feel like a personal attack.
sentences.zh: 第一点，为什么反馈会让人感觉像是一种人身攻击。

sentences.en: I think it's that it often kind of hits us in our tender spots.
sentences.zh: 我认为是因为它往往触及了我们脆弱的地方。

sentences.en: It can feel like it's an indication that we are lacking in some way, that we are not enough.
sentences.zh: 它可能让人觉得这是一种暗示，表明我们在某些方面有所欠缺，我们还不够好。

sentences.en: And that can trigger all sorts of
sentences.zh: 这可能会触发各种

sentences.en: current, past, present imaginings.
sentences.zh: 过去、现在和当下的想象。

sentences.en: You know, I'm going to lose my job or, you know, they're going to break up with me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，比如“我要丢掉工作了”，或者“他们要和我分手了”。

sentences.en: You know, I'm not good enough.
sentences.zh: 你知道，“我做得不够好”。

sentences.en: Others are better.
sentences.zh: “别人比我强”。

sentences.en: I'm not going to get the pay rise that I need.
sentences.zh: “我拿不到我需要的加薪”。

sentences.en: You know, there can be so many aspects built in.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其中可能包含很多方面。

sentences.en: And it might also be traumatic things about when people have told you things in not the kindest of ways in the past, that it all comes screaming back to you in the present.
sentences.zh: 这可能还涉及一些创伤性事件，比如过去有人以不友善的方式对你说过某些话，现在这一切又像尖叫一样回到了你的脑海中。

sentences.en: It might really tap into your self-worth.
sentences.zh: 它可能真的触及了你的自我价值感。

sentences.en: It might make you feel that you are not good enough.
sentences.zh: 它可能让你觉得你不够好。

sentences.en: You are not enough.
sentences.zh: 你还不够好。

sentences.en: We've also got to remember that we've got those fantastic, tricky human brains of ours as well.
sentences.zh: 我们还必须记住，我们拥有那些奇妙而又棘手的人类大脑。

sentences.en: And that being cast out can feel really, really threatening.
sentences.zh: 被排斥的感觉真的会让人感到非常威胁。

sentences.en: And that it might well get our fight and flight system into full swing that makes us feel vulnerable and like our position in society or our pack is at risk.
sentences.zh: 这很可能会全面启动我们的“战斗或逃跑”系统，让我们感到脆弱，觉得我们在社会或群体中的地位岌岌可危。

sentences.en: As a result of that, you might notice physical sensations in your body when you're being offered feedback.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你收到反馈时，你可能会注意到身体上的感觉。

sentences.en: That might include gurgling stomach.
sentences.zh: 这可能包括胃部翻腾。

sentences.en: It might include feeling like you need to run to the loo.
sentences.zh: 可能包括感觉需要跑去洗手间。

sentences.en: It really can feel awful.
sentences.zh: 这真的会让人感觉很糟糕。

sentences.en: You might find that it makes you feel physically hot, sweaty, flushed.
sentences.zh: 你可能会发现它让你感到身体发热、出汗、脸红。

sentences.en: It can be very physically uncomfortable indeed.
sentences.zh: 这确实可能在生理上让人非常不舒服。

sentences.en: Not always, but sometimes.
sentences.zh: 不总是这样，但有时会。

sentences.en: And of course, that might be for good reason.
sentences.zh: 当然，这可能是有充分理由的。

sentences.en: This might be fear that's being elicited.
sentences.zh: 这可能是被激发的恐惧。

sentences.en: It might be something that's been so super hard in the past that it gets your pattern matching receptors firing
sentences.zh: 这可能是过去发生过非常艰难的事情，导致你的模式匹配受体被激活，

sentences.en: and makes you feel vulnerable and like it's going to happen all over again.
sentences.zh: 让你感到脆弱，觉得这一切又要重演了。

sentences.en: Even what they call constructive feedback can trigger this response and make us feel like we are not good enough.
sentences.zh: 即使是所谓的建设性反馈，也可能触发这种反应，让我们觉得我们不够好。

sentences.en: And of course, this can be exacerbated, made even worse with the temperature of our internal self-talk, the way we talk about ourselves.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果我们内心自我对话的基调——即我们谈论自己的方式——很糟糕，这种情况会进一步加剧。

sentences.en: If it feeds into what you already think about yourself, that's when this can feel like a massive sledgehammer blow.
sentences.zh: 如果它迎合了你对自己已有的负面看法，那就会感觉像是一记沉重的重锤打击。

sentences.en: So this brings us pretty nicely onto point two, why we would be avoiding of feedback from others.
sentences.zh: 这很好地引出了第二点，为什么我们会回避他人的反馈。

sentences.en: Well, having looked at section one and the responses that we might well be experiencing, it doesn't really feel that wild that we'd want to avoid
sentences.zh: 好吧，在看了第一部分以及我们可能经历的反应后，我们想要避免

sentences.en: experiencing all of that.
sentences.zh: 经历这一切，这并不奇怪。

sentences.en: And so we might not want to receive feedback from others.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可能不想接受他人的反馈。

sentences.en: But let's take a quick look at some of the reasons why we might feel like we want to avoid that feedback.
sentences.zh: 但让我们快速看看我们可能想要回避反馈的一些原因。

sentences.en: Well, it might be a fear of shame or humiliation, perhaps fear of confirming our worst thoughts or doubts about
sentences.zh: 好吧，这可能是对羞耻或羞辱的恐惧，也许是害怕证实我们对自己最糟糕的想法或怀疑，

sentences.en: ourselves, past experiences where feedback was delivered poorly or unkindly.
sentences.zh: 或者是过去反馈交付得很差或不友善的经历。

sentences.en: There is something called RSD, rejection sensitive dysphoria.
sentences.zh: 有一种东西叫做 RSD，即“拒绝敏感性焦虑”。

sentences.en: That's where it feels even more painful or uncomfortable to receive feedback.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，接受反馈会让人感觉更加痛苦或不舒服。

sentences.en: And where it might always feel like it's critical, like it's kind of stripping you down to the bone, like it's making you want to run away and hide.
sentences.zh: 而且它总是让人觉得这是一种批评，好像把你剥得体无完肤，让你想要逃跑和躲藏。

sentences.en: You know, those thoughts are spiralling, making you feel like others are better.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些想法在盘旋，让你觉得别人比你更好。

sentences.en: You know, you should never have done this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你本不该做这件事。

sentences.en: Who am I to think I could do this?
sentences.zh: 我是谁，竟然认为我能做到这一点？

sentences.en: Makes you want to just bury your head in the sand and never come up for air again.
sentences.zh: 让你只想把头埋进沙子里，再也不要出来透气。

sentences.en: And that can be something that is commonly experienced by people with an ADHD diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 这可能是被诊断为多动症（ADHD）的人经常经历的事情。

sentences.en: If you'd find a standalone episode on RSD helpful, please do drop me a comment or connect with me on socials and let me know.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得关于 RSD 的独立一集会有帮助，请给我留言或在社交媒体上与我联系，让我知道。

sentences.en: Okay, number three, how do we begin to be able to receive feedback without falling apart?
sentences.zh: 好的，第三点，我们如何开始在不崩溃的情况下接受反馈？

sentences.en: So my number one tip is to try to stay in the moment.
sentences.zh: 所以我的第一条建议是尝试活在当下。

sentences.en: And one of the best ways we can do that is by just taking a moment to pause, make sure you are breathing, make sure you're not holding
sentences.zh: 做到这一点最好的方法之一就是花点时间停下来，确保你在呼吸，确保你没有屏住

sentences.en: your breath, because that's when the body might start to go into fight and flight.
sentences.zh: 呼吸，因为那样身体可能会开始进入“战斗或逃跑”状态。

sentences.en: So we want to try and keep you mindful of being in this moment so that you don't begin to dissociate, you don't begin to start a panic cycle.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想让你保持正念，活在当下，这样你就不会开始解离，不会开始陷入恐慌循环。

sentences.en: So once you start to realise that you're receiving feedback, just take a breath breath in through your nose, hold that for a moment, breathe out through your mouth.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你意识到你正在接受反馈，只需深吸一口气，屏住片刻，然后通过嘴呼出。

sentences.en: Don't feel that you need to rush in to defend yourself.
sentences.zh: 不要觉得你需要急于为自己辩护。

sentences.en: Sometimes we just need to be able to listen, to hear.
sentences.zh: 有时我们只需要能够倾听，去听。

sentences.en: And that's something that I find really helpful trying to remind myself when I'm parenting as well.
sentences.zh: 这也是我在育儿时发现非常有帮助的一点，我试着提醒自己。

sentences.en: Sometimes I just need to listen, I don't need to fix, I just need to hear.
sentences.zh: 有时我只需要倾听，不需要去解决，我只需要去听。

sentences.en: Once we begin to be able to pause, to slow things down a bit, that's when we might be able to begin to separate the feedback from our self-worth.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们开始能够停下来，让事情慢下来一点，我们或许就能开始将反馈与我们的自我价值分离开来。

sentences.en: To know that one piece of feedback doesn't define you.
sentences.zh: 要知道，一条反馈并不能定义你。

sentences.en: You know, I guess even with this podcast, some people might be like, oh, it's terrible, you're awful, you know, I hate the sound of your voice, you're dreadful.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想即使是这个播客，有些人可能会说，哦，这太糟糕了，你太差劲了，你知道，我讨厌你的声音，你太可怕了。

sentences.en: But actually, they might not be the person this podcast is created for.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他们可能并不是这个播客的目标受众。

sentences.en: And we might be able to think about their opinion, or I might be able to think about their opinion,
sentences.zh: 我们或许可以思考他们的观点，或者我或许可以思考他们的观点，

sentences.en: to be, you know, a signal that I'm not cut out for this, or that I should jack it all in, you know, quit.
sentences.zh: 认为，你知道，这是一个信号，表明我不适合做这个，或者我应该放弃这一切，你知道，辞职。

sentences.en: Sometimes I can just allow other people to hold opinions that might be different to
sentences.zh: 有时我可以允许其他人持有与我不同的观点，

sentences.en: my own, that might be different to, you know, what I wanted, or what others I hope might think about me.
sentences.zh: 可能与我想要的，或者我希望别人对我的看法不同。

sentences.en: We need to know that that piece of feedback doesn't define us, and that it might not also be true.
sentences.zh: 我们需要知道那条反馈并不能定义我们，而且它也可能不是事实。

sentences.en: Of course, it might be true.
sentences.zh: 当然，它可能是真的。

sentences.en: And we might need to be able to consider what changes we can make, how we might reframe what we're doing, do something a little bit differently, so that it
sentences.zh: 我们需要能够考虑我们可以做出什么改变，我们如何重构我们正在做的事情，做一些稍微不同的事情，以便它

sentences.en: better meets our needs and the needs of whoever it is we're trying to serve or kind of provide a service for.
sentences.zh: 更好地满足我们的需求，以及我们试图服务或提供服务的对象的需求。

sentences.en: And another tip can be starting to look for the useful grain.
sentences.zh: 另一个建议是开始寻找有用的部分。

sentences.en: So even if someone gives you kind of a vitriolic, you know, really not very nice version of their truth, it might be that we
sentences.zh: 所以即使有人给你一种尖酸刻薄的、真的不太友好的真相版本，我们也可能

sentences.en: can actually kind of dilute it down, almost like looking for if you were doing, I know in Australia,
sentences.zh: 实际上可以把它稀释一下，就像寻找——我知道在澳大利亚，

sentences.en: once I was looking in opal mines, and you were kind of getting like a sand sieve, and trying to sieve out all the dirt to look for the tiny opals.
sentences.zh: 有一次我在蛋白石矿里寻找，你就像拿着一个沙筛，试图筛掉所有的泥土来寻找微小的蛋白石。

sentences.en: And it might be that even within something that feels not very helpful, that there might be a really useful, tiny little shiny diamond or opal that maybe is
sentences.zh: 即使在感觉不太有用的东西中，也可能有一个非常有用的、微小的闪亮钻石或蛋白石，也许

sentences.en: useful for you to take on board.
sentences.zh: 对你来说是有用的，可以采纳。

sentences.en: So we can kind of almost discard some of the stuff that feels like actually, that's not kind, that's not helpful, and just really kind of reduce it down almost to look for
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以几乎丢弃那些感觉“实际上，那不友善，那没用”的东西，真正地把它精简下来，去寻找

sentences.en: anything that might be helpful in going forward, but doesn't feel so personal.
sentences.zh: 任何在未来可能有用，但感觉不那么针对个人的东西。

sentences.en: I love this next one.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢接下来这一点。

sentences.en: It is be curious, not furious.
sentences.zh: 那就是保持好奇，不要愤怒。

sentences.en: Can you begin to view this as information, but not a verdict?
sentences.zh: 你能开始把它视为信息，而不是判决吗？

sentences.en: We're literally with curiosity just looking at it, just taking a look at what it, you know, what it looks like, what it
sentences.zh: 我们真的只是带着好奇心看着它，只是看看它，你知道，它看起来是什么样，听起来是什么样，

sentences.en: sounds like, what it feels like, and you know, just trying to be a bit more zoomed out, a bit more objective.
sentences.zh: 感觉是什么样，你知道，只是试着把视角拉远一点，更客观一点。

sentences.en: So curious, not furious.
sentences.zh: 所以，好奇，不要愤怒。

sentences.en: We also need to be able to ask clarifying questions.
sentences.zh: 我们还需要能够提出澄清问题。

sentences.en: Now this is something that I probably wish I had done at one episode in my life, when somebody told me they didn't
sentences.zh: 这是我可能希望在生命中的某个阶段做过的事情，当时有人告诉我他们不喜欢

sentences.en: like my voice, and they found it to be the most painful experiences of their lives.
sentences.zh: 我的声音，他们觉得这是他们一生中最痛苦的经历之一。

sentences.en: I didn't ask for clarification in that moment, but I sure wish I had, because that person is no longer with us, and so my opportunity to do that has passed.
sentences.zh: 我当时没有要求澄清，但我真希望我当时做了，因为那个人已经不在了，所以我这样做的机会已经过去了。

sentences.en: I think nowadays I would be a better self-advocate.
sentences.zh: 我想现在我会是一个更好的自我倡导者。

sentences.en: I would be better at asking for clarification, and also knowing that I don't need to hold on to that.
sentences.zh: 我会更善于要求澄清，也知道我不需要纠结于此。

sentences.en: I kind of wish I hadn't, because I think it did keep me stuck for quite some years.
sentences.zh: 我有点希望我当时没有纠结，因为我认为这确实让我困住了好几年。

sentences.en: An example of a clarifying question might be, can you let me know what you think I could focus on to improve this?
sentences.zh: 一个澄清问题的例子可能是：你能告诉我你认为我可以专注于改进什么吗？

sentences.en: So I guess we're looking for things that are tangible, something that helps us to be able to make action steps, you know, something that makes it measurable.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜我们在寻找具体的东西，一些能帮助我们采取行动步骤的东西，你知道，一些让它可衡量的东西。

sentences.en: When we're looking at goal setting, we're looking at SMART goals.
sentences.zh: 当我们设定目标时，我们看的是 SMART 目标。

sentences.en: So something that's specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, and time focused.
sentences.zh: 所以要具体、可衡量、可实现、现实且有时间限制。

sentences.en: And that might be an approach that would work really well for garnering this feedback as well and putting that into action.
sentences.zh: 这可能也是一种非常适合收集反馈并将其付诸行动的方法。

sentences.en: We also need to begin to notice our triggers, you know, what really gets your goat, so to speak?
sentences.zh: 我们还需要开始注意我们的触发点，你知道，什么真正让你生气，可以这么说？

sentences.en: What are your tender spots?
sentences.zh: 你脆弱的地方在哪里？

sentences.en: Where are your Achilles heels?
sentences.zh: 你的阿喀琉斯之踵在哪里？

sentences.en: If it's always in the same spot, then it might be something that is kind of old stuff that's being brought to the front.
sentences.zh: 如果它总是出现在同一个地方，那么这可能是某种被带到前台的旧东西。

sentences.en: And it might be that we need to work through that in supervision, in a meeting with someone you care about, with a friend, a family, a loved one, or maybe even therapy too.
sentences.zh: 我们可能需要在督导中、在与你关心的人、朋友、家人、爱人的会议中，甚至在治疗中解决这个问题。

sentences.en: This can be where reflective journal writing comes in really helpfully as well too.
sentences.zh: 这也可以是反思性日记写作非常有帮助的地方。

sentences.en: Spend some time with yourself, really invite yourself to look at those tender spots and to think about what might have helped create them to begin with.
sentences.zh: 花点时间与自己相处，真正邀请自己去审视那些脆弱的地方，并思考是什么导致了它们的产生。

sentences.en: Number four, let's look at some practical exercises that might be really helpful to help feedback feel less triggering, less awful.
sentences.zh: 第四点，让我们看看一些可能非常有用的实用练习，帮助反馈感觉不那么具有触发性，不那么糟糕。

sentences.en: We need to reframe our feedback mentally.
sentences.zh: 我们需要在心理上重构我们的反馈。

sentences.en: It might be that we need to notice those thoughts and really name them as thoughts as well.
sentences.zh: 我们可能需要注意到那些想法，并真正把它们命名为“想法”。

sentences.en: So rather than having the thought that I'm not good enough, you know, we can be like, I'm having the thought that I'm not good enough.
sentences.zh: 所以与其产生“我不够好”的想法，你知道，我们可以说，我产生了“我不够好”的想法。

sentences.en: And maybe even shift, I'm not good enough to I'm learning, I'm trying to improve my skills, which can feel more positive and like you've got more hope and more scope.
sentences.zh: 甚至可以转变一下，从“我不够好”转变为“我正在学习，我正在努力提高我的技能”，这会感觉更积极，让你觉得有更多的希望和空间。

sentences.en: Keeping a feedback growth journal can be really transformational.
sentences.zh: 保持一本反馈成长日记可以带来真正的转变。

sentences.en: Write back any feedback that you've received and how you responded in that moment.
sentences.zh: 写下你收到的任何反馈以及你当时是如何回应的。

sentences.en: You might find it helpful to leave some blank spaces underneath so you can revisit so that
sentences.zh: 你可能会发现留出一些空白空间很有帮助，这样你就可以回顾，以便

sentences.en: your future self might have different thoughts, different ways of weighing in on that same problem.
sentences.zh: 未来的你可能会有不同的想法，有不同的方式来权衡同一个问题。

sentences.en: And you might actually one day be able to kind of cross it out and think, actually, that's done.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可能有一天能够把它划掉，心想，实际上，那已经完成了。

sentences.en: I've learned from that.
sentences.zh: 我从中吸取了教训。

sentences.en: I've incorporated that into my regular day to day interactions at work or in a home situation with a friend, with a colleague, with a loved one, a family member.
sentences.zh: 我已经把它融入到我日常的工作互动中，或者在家庭环境中，与朋友、同事、爱人、家庭成员的互动中。

sentences.en: And actually, that's not an issue for me anymore.
sentences.zh: 实际上，那对我来说不再是一个问题了。

sentences.en: Or you start to get feedback about how well you're doing at that thing.
sentences.zh: 或者你开始收到关于你在那件事上做得有多好的反馈。

sentences.en: And you're like, okay, job done.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，好的，任务完成。

sentences.en: This one might feel a little bit more of a struggle.
sentences.zh: 这一点可能感觉更挣扎一些。

sentences.en: And what we're definitely not doing here is we're not, we're not whitewashing.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里绝对不是在粉饰太平。

sentences.en: We're not using positive psychology to make it toxic.
sentences.zh: 我们不是在使用积极心理学让它变得有毒。

sentences.en: We're not gaslighting ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们不是在对自己进行煤气灯操纵。

sentences.en: But we might be able to be thinking about practicing a bit of gratitude.
sentences.zh: 但我们或许可以考虑练习一点感恩。

sentences.en: When someone's offering us feedback, hopefully in a constructive way, it's actually that they are invested in our development and they care about us and that they
sentences.zh: 当有人向我们提供反馈时，希望是以建设性的方式，实际上是他们投入了我们的发展，他们关心我们，他们

sentences.en: think we can perhaps do better.
sentences.zh: 认为我们或许可以做得更好。

sentences.en: That is someone who is invested in you.
sentences.zh: 那是一个为你投入的人。

sentences.en: Even if it might feel hostile, they want you to thrive.
sentences.zh: 即使它可能感觉带有敌意，他们也希望你茁壮成长。

sentences.en: They want you to soar.
sentences.zh: 他们希望你展翅高飞。

sentences.en: And being able to hold on to that.
sentences.zh: 并能够坚持这一点。

sentences.en: And like I said, with that sieve, sieving it out to find the useful nuggets, the useful grains of truth that you
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，用那个筛子，把它筛出来，找到有用的金块，那些你觉得有用的真理的颗粒，

sentences.en: can hold on to and that do feel comfortable enough to hold on to and to transform and act upon is really key.
sentences.zh: 你可以坚持下去，并且觉得足够舒服去坚持、去转化、去付诸行动，这才是关键。

sentences.en: So have you found this helpful?
sentences.zh: 那么，你觉得这有帮助吗？

sentences.en: What's been your take home point?
sentences.zh: 你最大的收获是什么？

sentences.en: Please do let me know in the comments.
sentences.zh: 请务必在评论区告诉我。

sentences.en: And if you've got any other advice, please do drop that in the comments.
sentences.zh: 如果你还有其他建议，也请务必写在评论区。

sentences.en: And if that resonates with you as a watcher or a viewer or a listener, please do support other people in the comments as well.
sentences.zh: 如果你作为观众或听众对此有共鸣，也请在评论区多多支持其他人。

sentences.en: If you find this content helpful, the kindest thing you can do is to follow the show on whatever platform you are watching or listening to or subscribe if you're on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得这些内容有帮助，你能做的最暖心的事，就是在你观看或收听的平台上关注这个节目，或者如果你在 YouTube 上观看，就订阅它。

sentences.en: Every like on YouTube helps YouTube to know this content is helpful and helps it to be discovered by a wider audience.
sentences.zh: YouTube 上的每一个点赞都能帮助平台了解这些内容是有用的，并帮助它被更多受众发现。

sentences.en: So please, if you're watching, especially at this point when we're on the finishing lap, please do drop me a like, please do drop me a comment.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你正在观看，特别是在我们即将结束的时候，请务必给我点个赞，留个言。

sentences.en: And if you're not already subscribed, please do me that kindness.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅，请务必帮我这个忙。

sentences.en: It really is the kindest thing you can do for any podcaster or content creator that you rate.
sentences.zh: 这真的是你能为你所认可的播客或内容创作者所做的最暖心的事了。

sentences.en: I would love to know what other content you would find helpful.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道你还觉得哪些内容会有帮助。

sentences.en: Please do let me know.
sentences.zh: 请务必告诉我。

sentences.en: Come and connect with me on socials where I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, absolutely everywhere.
sentences.zh: 欢迎在社交媒体上与我联系，我的名字是 Marianne Trent 博士，在所有平台上都是这个名字。

sentences.en: And please do, if you're an aspiring psychologist, come and join my free
sentences.zh: 如果你是一位有抱负的心理学家，请务必加入我的免费

sentences.en: Facebook group, the aspiring psychologist community with Dr. Marianne Trent, which is the exclusive
sentences.zh: Facebook 群组，“Marianne Trent 博士的心理学家成长社区”，这里是

sentences.en: home of Marianne's motivation and mindset sessions, which happen on Friday mornings.
sentences.zh: Marianne 的动力与思维课程的专属基地，课程在每周五早上进行。

sentences.en: If you're looking to become a psychologist, then let this be your guide.
sentences.zh: 如果你想成为一名心理学家，那就让这成为你的指南吧。

sentences.en: With this podcast, you'll be on your way to being qualified.
sentences.zh: 有了这个播客，你离获得资格就不远了。

sentences.en: It's the aspiring psychologist podcast with Dr. Marianne Trent.
sentences.zh: 这就是由 Marianne Trent 博士主持的“心理学家成长播客”。

sentences.en: Did I ever tell you about the time I earned £300 whilst I was at a Pilates class?
sentences.zh: 我有没有告诉过你，有一次我在上普拉提课时赚了 300 英镑？

sentences.en: And no, spoiler alert, I wasn't teaching the Pilates.
sentences.zh: 不，剧透一下，我当时并不是在教普拉提。

sentences.en: It was money coming into my business whilst I was doing something completely different.
sentences.zh: 那是我在做完全不同的事情时，我的生意里进账的钱。

sentences.en: If you've ever wondered how you might create income that isn't directly tied to your time, there's a free challenge starting on the 2nd of November.
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经想过如何创造不直接与你的时间挂钩的收入，那么 11 月 2 日将有一个免费的挑战赛开始。

sentences.en: It's called The Race to Recurring Revenue.
sentences.zh: 它叫“循环收入竞赛”。

sentences.en: It's hosted by Sophie Foote, and I'd love you to join through my link so I can support you too.
sentences.zh: 它由 Sophie Foote 主持，我很希望你能通过我的链接加入，这样我也能支持你。

sentences.en: The details are in the show notes, or you can drop me a DM via socials.
sentences.zh: 详细信息在节目说明里，或者你可以通过社交媒体给我发私信。

sentences.en: Now on with the show.
sentences.zh: 现在，节目继续。
